scope: Independent AI Golden SOP editorial review of eight provisional Author A drafts; no human, media, device or live approval.

checks.build: Fresh build and --check pass: 8 lessons, 48 questions, 32 audio requests, 0 structural flags.
checks.sourceAndTarget: All eight occurrence IDs, expressions and full source sentences match source-inventory.jsonl, and each reviewed target regex matches the cited source sentence. Every dialogue key and both writing examples per lesson contain a target match.
checks.reply: Every four-option reply set has exactly one target-bearing golden option; the four choices were read for independent pragmatic truth in their shared scene.
checks.glossaryAndSpeaking: All 40 glossary entries are exact suggested-answer spans after permitted case normalization and exclude the target; all eight speaking offsets slice the target form.
checks.audio: Four requested audio texts per lesson are distinct and target-bearing; synthesis, voice and playback were not checked.
checks.bilingual: English and Traditional Chinese task, option, model and takeaway claims were compared; no additional factual mismatch identified.

findings.evidence: The scene has a shopper enter a stationery shop for glue, see a checkout offer and buy unplanned cups. Final writing has a student enter a convenience shop for water, see a checkout offer and buy unplanned sweets. Both use the same checkout-promotion trigger, same single-item shopping trip and same add-on purchase decision; only the shop and products change.
findings.problem: The final task does not require meaningful transfer to a changed context as required by SOP P85 and the final writing step.
findings.repair: Move final writing to a distinctly different trigger and setting, such as a museum visitor who had planned only to see an exhibition but suddenly buys a print after viewing a painting. Avoid another checkout promotion or the bus-app trigger already used in listening; regenerate both model answers, translations and exact answer-derived glossary spans.

findings.evidence: The dialogue is a mother with childhood memories of visiting an old bakery with her grandmother despite long queues. Final writing is an alumna with school-day breakfast memories at a small bakery despite cheaper alternatives. Both ask the learner to apply a soft spot for to nostalgic attachment to an old bakery with an acknowledged downside.
findings.problem: The new-setting task repeats the immediately prior dialogue's place, emotion and concession structure, limiting transfer across contexts.
findings.repair: Use a different object or person of affection in final writing, with a different concrete reason and reasonable imperfection; then revise both English models, Traditional Chinese translations and their 4–6 exact answer-derived glossary rows.

findings.evidence: The form list says ‘a break or action could/do/does/did a world of good’. The slash notation treats could as parallel to finite lexical forms, leaving the ungrammatical reading ‘a break could a world of good’.
findings.problem: The scalable grammar brief should explicitly encode the modal-plus-verb construction for authors and reviewers.
findings.repair: Write ‘could do / may do / does / did a world of good’ and keep the existing do someone a world of good variant. This metadata repair need not change assessed strings.

conclusion: Repair lessons 2618 and 2649 for genuine changed-context writing; clarify lesson 2672 grammar notation. The other five lessons had no independent editorial finding in this pass. All eight remain provisional.
